title: Suresh Auto Parts v. Narayan Gupta
full_text: FACTS: Narayan Gupta issued a cheque of Rs. 75,000 to Suresh Auto Parts against supply of spare parts. The cheque bounced due to 'insufficient funds'. The statutory notice was sent by the complainant's counsel by speed post, but the notice was returned with the remark 'addressee left without instructions'. The complainant filed the complaint under Section 138 without re-sending the notice to any alternate address, though one was known and available on invoices exchanged between the parties. ISSUE: Whether service of notice at only one known address, when an alternate address was available to the complainant, satisfies the requirement of Section 138 proviso (b). REASONING: The court distinguished this case from situations where the accused deliberately evades service. Since the complainant possessed a second address (on the invoice) but made no attempt to serve notice there despite the first attempt failing, the court held that reasonable diligence in effecting service had not been demonstrated. The court referred to the general principle that the notice requirement under Section 138 is not a mere formality but a substantive precondition giving the drawer an opportunity to pay before criminal liability attaches. HOLDING: The complaint was held not maintainable for failure to properly serve the demand notice, and the accused was acquitted. The court clarified that this does not bar the complainant from pursuing civil remedies for recovery of the amount.
